technical_terms.how_marx_uses_it: The useful quality of a thing, which exists only through its physical properties and its use or consumption.
The quantitative proportion in which one use value is exchanged for another; the form in which value appears.
The congealed, homogeneous human labour embodied in a commodity, distinct from its use value.
Labour with its concrete useful form abstracted away, counting only as expenditure of human labour power.
Labour considered qualitatively, as it makes a particular use value (tailoring, weaving).
The human capacity to work, spent in production; what abstract labour expends.
Labour time needed under normal conditions with average skill and intensity; it sets the magnitude of value.
The quantity of value, measured by labour time, as distinct from its form.
Unskilled average labour; skilled labour counts as multiplied simple labour.
Value as the solidified residue of human labour, a crystal of one social substance.
The social form in which value appears, separate from the commodity's physical form.
The pole of the value expression in which a commodity's value is expressed through another commodity.
The pole in which another commodity serves as the material that expresses the first commodity's value.
The simplest value relation: x commodity A = y commodity B.

technical_terms.term: total or expanded form of value
technical_terms.how_marx_uses_it: Form B: one commodity's value expressed in an open-ended series of other commodities.
Form C: all commodities express value in one common commodity, making value socially visible.
The commodity whose body serves as the common equivalent of all others; the step toward money.
Form D: the general value form fixed on one commodity (gold) as money.
The money expression of a commodity's value, a relation to gold that exists in thought.
The commodity (here gold) that holds the universal equivalent role.

technical_terms.term: measure of value / standard of price
technical_terms.how_marx_uses_it: Money's first function, expressing values as same-denomination magnitudes; distinct from the standard of price, a fixed weight.
Money used only in thought to express prices, with no real gold changing hands.
Money as a reckoning unit that fixes the value of a commodity in money form.
The appearance that social relations between producers take the form of relations between things.
A product of labour as a sign whose social meaning must be deciphered.
Labour done independently by private producers, whose social character appears only in exchange.
An object outside us that satisfies wants and is made for exchange; the unit of capitalist wealth.
Labour is both concrete (making use values) and abstract (making value) at once.
Classical economy studies the real relations of production; vulgar economy describes appearances.

recurring_phrases.meaning: Value as labour time solidified in the product.
Labour stripped of its useful form; the substance of value.

recurring_phrases.phrase: bodily form becomes its value form
recurring_phrases.meaning: The equivalent's physical body takes on the role of expressing another commodity's value.
The equivalent's body reflects the value of the relative commodity.
Money's puzzle is the puzzle of commodities in a sharper form.
Money used only in thought to fix prices.
A form value takes only through the social relations of all commodities.
A commodity is useless to its owner, who wants to trade it for useful goods.
Relations between producers appearing as relations between products.
The relative form acts; the equivalent form is passive.

hegelian_or_philosophical.meaning_in_context: Relational concepts (king and subjects) whose meaning depends on the relation; Hegel's term, applied to value.
Exchange value as the appearance of a substance contained in commodities.
Labour time as the measure inherent in commodities, expressed as money.
Ironic: the leap from necessity to freedom, hard for a commodity to make from imaginary to real gold.
Hegel's view that the valuable thing counts for what it is worth; cited on money as symbol.
The common substance, labour, that manifests itself in exchange value.
Proudhon's 'justice eternelle', mocked as an ideal drawn from commodity production.

Footnote on Jerome's vision, used to joke about a commodity's transformation into money.

voice_attribution_risks.note: Parenthesis inserted by Engels (fn12, 4th German edition) sits inside Marx's text and could read as Marx's own.
Opens with 'Some people might think...' (opponent's view) before Marx's answer; easy to misread.
Footnote 16 has Adam Smith's view, then Marx's assessment, then Engels's bracketed note on Work vs Labour.
Footnote 21 quotes Broadhurst at length then mocks him; Engels's bracketed note ends it.
Satirical portrait of mercantilists and free-trade 'bagmen'; irony that could be taken as a claim.
Footnote 26 mixes Proudhon's ideal, Marx's joke about popes and Catholics, and Goethe; reader must track each voice.
Footnote 26a is an editors' (MECW) note from the German edition, not Marx.
Footnote 34 quotes Marx's own 1847 book, and footnotes 32-33 argue with Ricardo's text as quoted.
Block quote of an economist's view; Marx's reply follows in the commodities' voice.
Many quoted authors (Locke, Law, Galiani) presented in sequence; some are opponents, others support.
Economists' view ('discoverers of this chemical element') is presented as theirs; Marx's answer is in the same paragraph.
